extracted.intended_audience: Users and potential contributors to the Metamath set.mm repository (formal-math / theorem-proving community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for creating, verifying, and submitting Metamath databases and proofs (especially for set.mm and related primary databases). Describes required verification, verifier roles, repository practices, and the principal included databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-step justification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove a theorem, every proof step must be proven using an axiom or a previously proven theorem; as a result, nothing is hidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every individual proof step in the database must be justified by an axiom or an earlier theorem; this is the core Metamath verification discipline ensuring fully explicit, checkable proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and minimal hard‑wired syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: The Metamath language is simple and robust, with an almost total absence of hard-wired syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Databases should express axioms, theorems, and proofs using the simple Metamath language design (avoid relying on system-specific hidden features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-readable axioms and theorem statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The resulting databases provide human-readable axioms and theorem statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Database entries should be written/maintained so that axioms and theorem statements are readable by humans (not only machine-encoded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof compression with decompressibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs in this repository are compressed to take relatively little space, but tools can easily decompress them to provide a human-readable sequence of every proof step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to store compressed proofs for space; however, tools must be able to expand them into the full sequence of steps for inspection and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-confidence correctness goal
rubrics_metrics.description: We work to provide extremely high confidence that the proofs are completely correct in these databases, especially for the set.mm and iset.mm databases (the primary databases under active development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality assurance and review practices should be aimed at maximizing confidence in correctness, particularly for the primary databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated commit verification before acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes ('commits') to any database are first automatically verified before they are accepted, using GitHub actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All commits must pass automated verification CI (GitHub Actions) prior to merge; contributions that fail automated checks should be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple independent verifier requirement for primary databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Every change to set.mm and iset.mm is verified by many independent verifiers, including metamath-exe, which also checks markup, and mmj2, which checks definition soundness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For set.mm and iset.mm, acceptance requires verification by multiple independent verifiers; metamath-exe and mmj2 are explicitly used to check markup and definition soundness respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-verifier verification for other databases
rubrics_metrics.description: All other databases' proofs are verified by one verifier (metamath-exe) in every commit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-primary databases require at minimum verification by metamath-exe on each commit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow CONTRIBUTING.md for contribution process and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: See CONTRIBUTING.md for more information on how to create a contribution, as well as how contributions are evaluated to decide if they will be merged in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors must follow the procedures, formatting, and evaluation criteria documented in CONTRIBUTING.md; that document governs how contributions are judged and merged.

rubrics_metrics.name: set.mm (Metamath Proof Explorer) axiomatic basis
rubrics_metrics.description: "set.mm" aka "Metamath Proof Explorer (MPE)" - uses classical logic and Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice (ZFC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: set.mm is the large, classical ZFC-based database; contributions intended for classical ZFC mathematics belong here and should conform to set.mm's conventions and verification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: iset.mm (Intuitionistic Logic Explorer) axiomatic basis
rubrics_metrics.description: "iset.mm" aka "Intuitionistic Logic Explorer" - uses intuitionistic set theory. In particular, it does not presume that the law of excluded middle is necessarily true in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions exploring intuitionistic logic and related mathematics should use iset.mm conventions and avoid assuming excluded middle.

rubrics_metrics.name: nf.mm (New Foundations Explorer) axiomatic basis
rubrics_metrics.description: "nf.mm" aka "New Foundations Explorer" - constructs mathematics using Quine's New Foundations (NF) set theory axioms, a direct derivative of the 'hierarchy of types' set theory originally presented in Principia Mathematica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nf.mm for developments based on Quine's NF axioms; follow that database's structure when contributing NF results.

rubrics_metrics.name: ql.mm (Quantum Logic Explorer) axiomatic basis
rubrics_metrics.description: "ql.mm" aka "Quantum Logic Explorer" - Starts from the orthomodular lattice properties proved in the Hilbert Space Explorer and takes you into quantum logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantum-logic developments should be placed in ql.mm and build upon the orthomodular lattice properties already present.

rubrics_metrics.name: hol.mm (Higher-Order Logic Explorer) axiomatic basis
rubrics_metrics.description: "hol.mm" aka "Higher-Order Logic Explorer" - Starts with higher-order logic (HOL, also called simple type theory) and derives equivalents to ZFC axioms, connecting the two approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HOL-based developments belong in hol.mm and may show relationships between HOL and ZFC within that database.

rubrics_metrics.name: peano.mm, big-unifier.mm, miu.mm, demo0.mm database descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: "peano.mm" - Peano arithmetic; "big-unifier.mm" - a unification and substitution test for Metamath verifiers (translation of William McCune's big-unifier.in); "miu.mm" - a simple formal system demonstration based on Hofstadter; "demo0.mm" - a simple formal system used as a demonstration in Chapter 2 of the Metamath book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These smaller/demo databases serve specialized/testing/demonstration roles and should be used accordingly when contributing or running verifier tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent verifiers and verifier documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many independent verifiers are used; metamath-exe checks markup, mmj2 checks definition soundness. For more information, see VERIFIERS.md.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should be aware of the roles of different verifiers and consult VERIFIERS.md to ensure their changes meet the checks performed by each verifier.
